How to learn — 3 rounds

Round 1 — Retrieve: Look at the picture and the meaning. Say the exact phrase out loud — every word, in the right order — then say the gapped sentence with the correct verb form (grind → ground, deal → dealt). Only then flip and check the phrase, the forms and the translation. Stuck? Use 💡 Hint before you flip — never flip “to peek”.
Round 2 — Sort: Mark each card I know it or Still learning (be honest — “know it” = you said it before flipping, without the hint). Then hit 🎯 Practise tricky ones and repeat until the tricky pile is empty. Too easy? Switch the front to 🖼️ Picture only.
Round 3 — Retell: No cards face-up! Retell how Rome's pressures combined (4+ Rome phrases), explain why one cause is not enough for the Maya (4+ Maya phrases), and argue which 3 ⚠️ causes mattered most. Bonus: use each phrase once about the modern world — “Traffic can grind to a halt…”

Pictures: from the “Empires & Evidence / Visual Vocabulary” lesson slides (Rome & Maya scenes) + AI illustrations for the ⚠️ Causes cards. History is more complex than any single metaphor — “deathblow” and “domino” images simplify a long process; they do not prove a single cause. We discuss the decline of some Classic Maya cities — not the disappearance of the Maya people.
